title.narrative: The effectiveness and quality of labour inspection systems and social dialogue institutions are strengthened

description.narrative:
The ILO supports ongoing efforts in Albania to strengthen occupational safety and health (OSH) and improve mechanisms for labour dispute resolution. Fatal work accidents remain high, while non-fatal incidents and occupational diseases are underreported. Psychological risks are recently integrated into national OSH policy document 2025-2030 endorsed in March 2025, and gaps persist in aligning legislation with EU directives. The absence of reliable accident data hinders evidence-based policymaking, and the State Labour Inspectorate requires strengthened capacities to enforce safety measures effectively. Simultaneously, Albania's labour dispute resolution system struggles with inefficiencies, leaving civil courts overloaded and many workers without timely access to justice. While mediation and conciliation mechanisms exist for collective disputes (3 out of 5 collective labour disputes were settled through Amicable Labour Dispute Resolution system in 2024), individual disputes lack structured alternatives, prolonging conflict resolution. Wages are not catching up with the rest of Europe and the big wage differences remain a main pull factor for labour emigration.
To address these challenges, the ILO supports Albania’s tripartite partners in the drafting and implementing the new OSH policy document 2025-2030 in developing a training curriculum in OSH and integrate this curriculum in a learning platform. Further, the ILO provides technical assistance to evaluate the possible effects that a change to the minimum wage system (from a unique level to sector levels) would bring in terms of labour market outcomes. These efforts aim to ensure safer working conditions, reduce work-related risks, tackle informality in the labour market and improve access to fair and efficient labour justice for all.
